svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Phospholipids scattered in water. The heads are hydrophilic; the tails are hydrophobic."], [1.5, "In water they arrange themselves so the tails are hidden from water."], [5, "A bilayer: tails face each other, heads face the water on both sides."], [8, "Bilayers can close into a liposome (vesicle); single layers can form micelles."]]
svg.title: Phospholipids in water
svg.desc: Phospholipids with hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails self-assemble in water into a micelle, a bilayer and a liposome.
svg.text: Phospholipids in water: micelle, bilayer and liposome

g.data-info: Hydrophilic phosphate head and two hydrophobic fatty-acid tails: amphipathic.
A sphere with heads outside and tails hidden inside; forms from single-tailed lipids (and some phospholipids) in water.
Two layers, tails facing inwards and heads facing the water on both sides: the basis of every cell membrane.
A bilayer that closes on itself into a hollow sphere with water inside; used to deliver drugs.
